  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

(3) TDD (RED failing test first → GREEN minimal implementation → REFACTOR); tests go in the standard unit-test tree only (Flutter/Dart `test/`, Node `__tests__/`/`test/`, Python `tests/`), NEVER in `testing/` (owned by test-automation agents; if production changes break tests there, leave them and note the breakage in outputs/response.md). Aim 100% coverage on new/modified code; include 2+ item cases for loop/collection behavior; run the FULL suite before finishing — no regressions. (4) Run git status, add .gitignore patterns for sensitive/untracked non-code files. (5) COMPLETION GUARD before writing the summary: `git fetch origin main && git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline` — EMPTY result means work did NOT land: re-do/resume, never report done from session memory or main's tip; same guard applies before any "no changes needed" conclusion (prove via `git log origin/main --grep` that the fix is genuinely on the base). (6) Write `outputs/response.md` as a concise PR description; post-processing handles branch/commit/PR.
- Output rules: `outputs/response.md` target under 20 lines; required sections `### What changed` (1–2 sentences), `### Key decisions` (bullets), `### How to verify` (test command); optional mermaid diagram inside `<details>`; no verbose ticket restatement, no filler. GitHub-flavored Markdown only — no Jira wiki markup (`{code}`, `{panel}`, `h1.`, `{{...}}`, `[title|url]`); if the issue references a parent/related issues, fetch with `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`.
- dmtools CLI: only for data NOT already in `input/`; commands include `jira_get_ticket`, `jira_search_by_jql`, `confluence_get_page_by_url`, `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_content_attachments <id>` (for attachments missing from input/), `ado_get_work_item`, `ado_search_work_items`, `github_get_issue`, `github_search_code`; handle errors gracefully; cite sources.
- Session ephemerality: one-shot ephemeral CI runner — when the final turn ends the process exits and the runner is destroyed; no timers/schedule_message/detached processes survive. Never end with work pending: long jobs run with `bash background: true` and polled via bash_job status/output between steps, or foreground if nothing else remains. The ONLY completion artifact is `outputs/response.md` written before exit; a missing response.md reads as "interrupted mid-way" (gh-742), resets the ticket, and re-runs the leg. Evidence fa#1341 (2026-10-07): a dev agent nohup'd `dart test &`, armed an 18-minute schedule_message wake-up, and ended its turn — the timer never fired, response.md was never written, and the leg failed twice with the same reset.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

messages.preview: While the baseline coverage run proceeds, let me draft the plan. First check job status:

blocks.text:
While the baseline runs, write the characterization tests (RED phase). But TDD says write failing test first — the characterization tests target helper functions that don't exist yet. I'll structure:

Phase 1: Write characterization tests in test_preCliReworkSetup.js covering the fail paths through `action` (these pass with current code — they're characterization tests of current behavior). Then refactor to helpers and export them; add direct tests for the new helpers? Direct helper tests would be RED first if helpers don't exist. The cleanest TDD order that works:

1. Write action-level characterization tests (RED doesn't apply — behavior already exists; characterization tests pass immediately, documenting behavior). 
2. Refactor: extract helpers (behavior preserved — action tests still green).
3. Add direct unit tests for exported helpers (can be done after; they exist by then — that's more "test-after" but acceptable; or export stubs first with failing tests... simpler to keep tests at action level plus helper-level after extraction).

Hmm, but the ticket AC: "characterization tests … then extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)". I'll write characterization tests first covering: setup failure paths (each failSetup branch), repoInfo failure, PR-anchor behavior, error reporting. Then extract helpers, keeping action tests green. Then maybe add direct helper tests to lock their behavior.

Test design — a shared makeMocks factory. Looking at existing test style, mocks are created inline per test. I'll add a `makeActionMocks(overides)` helper in the test file.

Key behaviors to test (characterization):

A. **No repoInfo** → action returns {success:false, error:'Could not resolve repository info from git remote (override via targetRepository in config).'} and tracker posts a comment containing the message (failSetup posts comment too). Note failSetup writes file too. Assert: result.success false, error contains 'Could not resolve', tracker.comments includes message.

B. **No PR found** (gh.findPRForTicket → null) → returns {success:false, error:'No PR found for ticket PROJ-123'}; file rework_setup_failed.md written containing the error; comment posted; error comment posted via reportActionError.

C. **PR details null** → error 'Could not get PR details for #7'.

D. **No branch name** (prDetails.head null) → error 'Could not determine branch name from PR #7'.

E. **Checkout throws** → error 'Failed to checkout branch'.

F. **Setup commands throw** → error 'Environment setup failed'.

G. **PR-anchored** (key pr-42): no findPRForTicket call, no tracker comment, returns success with prNumber 42. Also skips moveToStatus. Assert tracker.comments empty, prSearchCalls 0, moveCalls 0.

H. **prNumber from jobParams** when key isn't pr-N: jp.prNumber='7' → uses 7, no findPRForTicket.

I. **reportActionError when tracker creation also fails** — e.g. restoreFromReleases throws + tracker creation fails: action returns {success:false, error:...}; console.error logged; no crash. (tracker undefined in catch → fallback creation throws → logged). This covers the tracker-creation fallback in the catch. Note: configLoader.loadProjectConfig succeeds (needed), createTracker throws. Hmm, but in my mocks createTracker is `function() { return tracker; }` — if it throws, the error happens... where? The `var tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(...)` line is INSIDE the try. So error thrown there → catch → reportActionError(params, tracker /* undefined */, error) → fallback: tries createTracker again → throws → console.error 'Failed to create tracker for error comment'. Returns {success:false}. Good test.

J. **postReworkStartedComment throws** (non-fatal) → action still returns success. Covers the else-try-catch.

Also the setup warnings write path: buildSetupWarningsMarkdown returns warnings → file written with content; and write failure → console.warn. Cover both? Nice-to-have; includes setupResult warnings.

Also checkout with prDetails.head null: gh.getPRDetails returns {number:7, base:{ref:'main'}} without head → branch fail. For checkout-throws test, head present.

Order of mocks: note `gh.getPRDetails(scm, pr.number)` — pr from findPRForTicket mock. My mock findPRForTicket returns {number:7,...}.

Conflict files etc. all no-op.

Also note: `configLoader.paramsForConfigLoad` mock is used, and `configLoader.loadProjectConfig` returns config; `createScm` returns scm. `scm.getRemoteRepoInfo` returns null by default → for happy-path tests must return {owner:'acme', repo:'widgets'}. Wait — existing tests return repoInfo with { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? In existing happy tests, getRemoteRepoInfo is called and repoInfo used for return owner/repo. Existing tests don't assert owner... In existing mocks, getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return null; }? Let me check existing test file — in the gh-802 test makeMocks, getRemoteRepoInfo returns { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? Actually earlier reading showed: `getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }; }` in one mock. Yes (gh-799 test).

Now the refactor. Let me write the new module. I'll write the helpers carefully, preserving exact log lines and behavior.

One subtlety — `parseReworkParams`: in original, ticketKey = inputFolder.split('/').pop() — unchanged. But the reportActionError computes ticketKey again from params.inputFolderPath || params.jobParams.inputFolderPath — must keep that exact fallback logic there.

Another subtlety: original defines `const config` etc. — const in eval'd loadModule is fine as before. I'll use function declarations for helpers (hoisted).

Now check file_write availability: in the module, file_write is a host global. When loaded via loadModule with mocks, preamble declares var file_write = mock. In real dmtools environment, host provides file_write. Fine.

Console: global console — in GralJS, is console available in preCliReworkSetup? It's used already in the file; presumably host provides it. Fine.

Now, helper CC estimates and coverage: helpers will be called by action tests covering most paths. Additionally I'll add direct unit tests for helpers. Direct tests need module exports — I'll export all new helpers.

CRAP math check with istanbul branch coverage — the exact CRAP formula in crap4js: CRAP = CC² × (1 − cov)³ + CC. Coverage used is branch coverage of the function. If I cover ~all branches, CRAP ≈ CC. action CC after extraction: let me count decision points remaining:

1. outer try/catch: catch +1
2. restoreFromReleases try/catch: +1
3. repoInfo if: +1
4. `!pr`: +1
5. `!prDetails`: +1
6. `!branchName`: +1
7. head ternary: +1
8. base ternary: +1
9. headSha ternary: +1
10. contract try/catch: +1
11. questions try/catch: +1
12. prAnchor if: +1
13. parentContext try/catch: +1
14. customParams `||`: +1 (short-circuit)
15. parsed.actualParams ... inputFolderPath ternary is inside parseReworkParams — not in action. But `var customParams = (params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams) || parsed.actualParams.customParams;` — `&&` +1, `||` +1.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

Conflict files etc. all no-op.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

messages.preview: While the baseline coverage run proceeds, let me draft the plan. First check job status:

blocks.text:
While the baseline runs, write the characterization tests (RED phase). But TDD says write failing test first — the characterization tests target helper functions that don't exist yet. I'll structure:

Phase 1: Write characterization tests in test_preCliReworkSetup.js covering the fail paths through `action` (these pass with current code — they're characterization tests of current behavior). Then refactor to helpers and export them; add direct tests for the new helpers? Direct helper tests would be RED first if helpers don't exist. The cleanest TDD order that works:

1. Write action-level characterization tests (RED doesn't apply — behavior already exists; characterization tests pass immediately, documenting behavior). 
2. Refactor: extract helpers (behavior preserved — action tests still green).
3. Add direct unit tests for exported helpers (can be done after; they exist by then — that's more "test-after" but acceptable; or export stubs first with failing tests... simpler to keep tests at action level plus helper-level after extraction).

Hmm, but the ticket AC: "characterization tests … then extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)". I'll write characterization tests first covering: setup failure paths (each failSetup branch), repoInfo failure, PR-anchor behavior, error reporting. Then extract helpers, keeping action tests green. Then maybe add direct helper tests to lock their behavior.

Test design — a shared makeMocks factory. Looking at existing test style, mocks are created inline per test. I'll add a `makeActionMocks(overides)` helper in the test file.

Key behaviors to test (characterization):

A. **No repoInfo** → action returns {success:false, error:'Could not resolve repository info from git remote (override via targetRepository in config).'} and tracker posts a comment containing the message (failSetup posts comment too). Note failSetup writes file too. Assert: result.success false, error contains 'Could not resolve', tracker.comments includes message.

B. **No PR found** (gh.findPRForTicket → null) → returns {success:false, error:'No PR found for ticket PROJ-123'}; file rework_setup_failed.md written containing the error; comment posted; error comment posted via reportActionError.

C. **PR details null** → error 'Could not get PR details for #7'.

D. **No branch name** (prDetails.head null) → error 'Could not determine branch name from PR #7'.

E. **Checkout throws** → error 'Failed to checkout branch'.

F. **Setup commands throw** → error 'Environment setup failed'.

G. **PR-anchored** (key pr-42): no findPRForTicket call, no tracker comment, returns success with prNumber 42. Also skips moveToStatus. Assert tracker.comments empty, prSearchCalls 0, moveCalls 0.

H. **prNumber from jobParams** when key isn't pr-N: jp.prNumber='7' → uses 7, no findPRForTicket.

I. **reportActionError when tracker creation also fails** — e.g. restoreFromReleases throws + tracker creation fails: action returns {success:false, error:...}; console.error logged; no crash. (tracker undefined in catch → fallback creation throws → logged). This covers the tracker-creation fallback in the catch. Note: configLoader.loadProjectConfig succeeds (needed), createTracker throws. Hmm, but in my mocks createTracker is `function() { return tracker; }` — if it throws, the error happens... where? The `var tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(...)` line is INSIDE the try. So error thrown there → catch → reportActionError(params, tracker /* undefined */, error) → fallback: tries createTracker again → throws → console.error 'Failed to create tracker for error comment'. Returns {success:false}. Good test.

J. **postReworkStartedComment throws** (non-fatal) → action still returns success. Covers the else-try-catch.

Also the setup warnings write path: buildSetupWarningsMarkdown returns warnings → file written with content; and write failure → console.warn. Cover both? Nice-to-have; includes setupResult warnings.

Also checkout with prDetails.head null: gh.getPRDetails returns {number:7, base:{ref:'main'}} without head → branch fail. For checkout-throws test, head present.

Order of mocks: note `gh.getPRDetails(scm, pr.number)` — pr from findPRForTicket mock. My mock findPRForTicket returns {number:7,...}.

Conflict files etc. all no-op.

Also note: `configLoader.paramsForConfigLoad` mock is used, and `configLoader.loadProjectConfig` returns config; `createScm` returns scm. `scm.getRemoteRepoInfo` returns null by default → for happy-path tests must return {owner:'acme', repo:'widgets'}. Wait — existing tests return repoInfo with { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? In existing happy tests, getRemoteRepoInfo is called and repoInfo used for return owner/repo. Existing tests don't assert owner... In existing mocks, getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return null; }? Let me check existing test file — in the gh-802 test makeMocks, getRemoteRepoInfo returns { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? Actually earlier reading showed: `getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }; }` in one mock. Yes (gh-799 test).

Now the refactor. Let me write the new module. I'll write the helpers carefully, preserving exact log lines and behavior.

One subtlety — `parseReworkParams`: in original, ticketKey = inputFolder.split('/').pop() — unchanged. But the reportActionError computes ticketKey again from params.inputFolderPath || params.jobParams.inputFolderPath — must keep that exact fallback logic there.

Another subtlety: original defines `const config` etc. — const in eval'd loadModule is fine as before. I'll use function declarations for helpers (hoisted).

Now check file_write availability: in the module, file_write is a host global. When loaded via loadModule with mocks, preamble declares var file_write = mock. In real dmtools environment, host provides file_write. Fine.

Console: global console — in GralJS, is console available in preCliReworkSetup? It's used already in the file; presumably host provides it. Fine.

Now, helper CC estimates and coverage: helpers will be called by action tests covering most paths. Additionally I'll add direct unit tests for helpers. Direct tests need module exports — I'll export all new helpers.

CRAP math check with istanbul branch coverage — the exact CRAP formula in crap4js: CRAP = CC² × (1 − cov)³ + CC. Coverage used is branch coverage of the function. If I cover ~all branches, CRAP ≈ CC. action CC after extraction: let me count decision points remaining:

1. outer try/catch: catch +1
2. restoreFromReleases try/catch: +1
3. repoInfo if: +1
4. `!pr`: +1
5. `!prDetails`: +1
6. `!branchName`: +1
7. head ternary: +1
8. base ternary: +1
9. headSha ternary: +1
10. contract try/catch: +1
11. questions try/catch: +1
12. prAnchor if: +1
13. parentContext try/catch: +1

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.

Conflict files etc. all no-op.

(6) Write `outputs/response.md` as a concise PR description; post-processing handles branch/commit/PR.

- Session ephemerality: one-shot ephemeral CI runner — when the final turn ends the process exits and the runner is destroyed; no timers/schedule_message/detached processes survive. Never end with work pending: long jobs run with `bash background: true` and polled via bash_job status/output between steps, or foreground if nothing else remains. The ONLY completion artifact is `outputs/response.md` written before exit; a missing response.md reads as "interrupted mid-way" (gh-742), resets the ticket, and re-runs the leg. Evidence fa#1341 (2026-10-07): a dev agent nohup'd `dart test &`, armed an 18-minute schedule_message wake-up, and ended its turn — the timer never fired, response.md was never written, and the leg failed twice with the same reset.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

While the baseline runs, write the characterization tests (RED phase). But TDD says write failing test first — the characterization tests target helper functions that don't exist yet. I'll structure:

Phase 1: Write characterization tests in test_preCliReworkSetup.js covering the fail paths through `action` (these pass with current code — they're characterization tests of current behavior). Then refactor to helpers and export them; add direct tests for the new helpers? Direct helper tests would be RED first if helpers don't exist. The cleanest TDD order that works:

1. Write action-level characterization tests (RED doesn't apply — behavior already exists; characterization tests pass immediately, documenting behavior). 
2. Refactor: extract helpers (behavior preserved — action tests still green).
3. Add direct unit tests for exported helpers (can be done after; they exist by then — that's more "test-after" but acceptable; or export stubs first with failing tests... simpler to keep tests at action level plus helper-level after extraction).

Hmm, but the ticket AC: "characterization tests … then extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)". I'll write characterization tests first covering: setup failure paths (each failSetup branch), repoInfo failure, PR-anchor behavior, error reporting. Then extract helpers, keeping action tests green. Then maybe add direct helper tests to lock their behavior.

Test design — a shared makeMocks factory. Looking at existing test style, mocks are created inline per test. I'll add a `makeActionMocks(overides)` helper in the test file.

Key behaviors to test (characterization):

A. **No repoInfo** → action returns {success:false, error:'Could not resolve repository info from git remote (override via targetRepository in config).'} and tracker posts a comment containing the message (failSetup posts comment too). Note failSetup writes file too. Assert: result.success false, error contains 'Could not resolve', tracker.comments includes message.

B. **No PR found** (gh.findPRForTicket → null) → returns {success:false, error:'No PR found for ticket PROJ-123'}; file rework_setup_failed.md written containing the error; comment posted; error comment posted via reportActionError.

C. **PR details null** → error 'Could not get PR details for #7'.

D. **No branch name** (prDetails.head null) → error 'Could not determine branch name from PR #7'.

E. **Checkout throws** → error 'Failed to checkout branch'.

F. **Setup commands throw** → error 'Environment setup failed'.

G. **PR-anchored** (key pr-42): no findPRForTicket call, no tracker comment, returns success with prNumber 42. Also skips moveToStatus. Assert tracker.comments empty, prSearchCalls 0, moveCalls 0.

H. **prNumber from jobParams** when key isn't pr-N: jp.prNumber='7' → uses 7, no findPRForTicket.

I. **reportActionError when tracker creation also fails** — e.g. restoreFromReleases throws + tracker creation fails: action returns {success:false, error:...}; console.error logged; no crash. (tracker undefined in catch → fallback creation throws → logged). This covers the tracker-creation fallback in the catch. Note: configLoader.loadProjectConfig succeeds (needed), createTracker throws. Hmm, but in my mocks createTracker is `function() { return tracker; }` — if it throws, the error happens... where? The `var tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(...)` line is INSIDE the try. So error thrown there → catch → reportActionError(params, tracker /* undefined */, error) → fallback: tries createTracker again → throws → console.error 'Failed to create tracker for error comment'. Returns {success:false}. Good test.

J. **postReworkStartedComment throws** (non-fatal) → action still returns success. Covers the else-try-catch.

Also the setup warnings write path: buildSetupWarningsMarkdown returns warnings → file written with content; and write failure → console.warn. Cover both? Nice-to-have; includes setupResult warnings.

Also checkout with prDetails.head null: gh.getPRDetails returns {number:7, base:{ref:'main'}} without head → branch fail. For checkout-throws test, head present.

Order of mocks: note `gh.getPRDetails(scm, pr.number)` — pr from findPRForTicket mock. My mock findPRForTicket returns {number:7,...}.

Conflict files etc. all no-op.

Also note: `configLoader.paramsForConfigLoad` mock is used, and `configLoader.loadProjectConfig` returns config; `createScm` returns scm. `scm.getRemoteRepoInfo` returns null by default → for happy-path tests must return {owner:'acme', repo:'widgets'}. Wait — existing tests return repoInfo with { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? In existing happy tests, getRemoteRepoInfo is called and repoInfo used for return owner/repo. Existing tests don't assert owner... In existing mocks, getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return null; }? Let me check existing test file — in the gh-802 test makeMocks, getRemoteRepoInfo returns { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }? Actually earlier reading showed: `getRemoteRepoInfo: function() { return { owner: 'acme', repo: 'widgets' }; }` in one mock. Yes (gh-799 test).

Now the refactor. Let me write the new module. I'll write the helpers carefully, preserving exact log lines and behavior.

One subtlety — `parseReworkParams`: in original, ticketKey = inputFolder.split('/').pop() — unchanged. But the reportActionError computes ticketKey again from params.inputFolderPath || params.jobParams.inputFolderPath — must keep that exact fallback logic there.

Another subtlety: original defines `const config` etc. — const in eval'd loadModule is fine as before. I'll use function declarations for helpers (hoisted).

Now check file_write availability: in the module, file_write is a host global. When loaded via loadModule with mocks, preamble declares var file_write = mock. In real dmtools environment, host provides file_write. Fine.

Console: global console — in GralJS, is console available in preCliReworkSetup? It's used already in the file; presumably host provides it. Fine.

Now, helper CC estimates and coverage: helpers will be called by action tests covering most paths. Additionally I'll add direct unit tests for helpers. Direct tests need module exports — I'll export all new helpers.

CRAP math check with istanbul branch coverage — the exact CRAP formula in crap4js: CRAP = CC² × (1 − cov)³ + CC. Coverage used is branch coverage of the function. If I cover ~all branches, CRAP ≈ CC. action CC after extraction: let me count decision points remaining:

ternary +1, `||` (prNumber/pr) +1, `||` +1. Total ≈ 1+5 = 6 → CRAP 6 covered; if uncovered 42 — exceeds 8! AC: "Newly introduced functions must sit at or below the same threshold (8)".   crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

messages.preview: While the baseline coverage run proceeds, let me draft the plan. First check job status:

blocks.text:
While the baseline runs, write the characterization tests (RED phase). But TDD says write failing test first — the characterization tests target helper functions that don't exist yet. I'll structure:

Phase 1: Write characterization tests in test_preCliReworkSetup.js covering the fail paths through `action` (these pass with current code — they're characterization tests of current behavior). Then refactor to helpers and export them; add direct tests for the new helpers? Direct helper tests would be RED first if helpers don't exist. The cleanest TDD order that works:

1. Write action-level characterization tests (RED doesn't apply — behavior already exists; characterization tests pass immediately, documenting behavior). 
2. Refactor: extract helpers (behavior preserved — action tests still green).
3. Add direct unit tests for exported helpers (can be done after; they exist by then — that's more "test-after" but acceptable; or export stubs first with failing tests... simpler to keep tests at action level plus helper-level after extraction).

Hmm, but the ticket AC: "characterization tests … then extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*)". I'll write characterization tests first covering: setup failure paths (each failSetup branch), repoInfo failure, PR-anchor behavior, error reporting. Then extract helpers, keeping action tests green. Then maybe add direct helper tests to lock their behavior.

Test design — a shared makeMocks factory. Looking at existing test style, mocks are created inline per test. I'll add a `makeActionMocks(overides)` helper in the test file.

Key behaviors to test (characterization):

A. **No repoInfo** → action returns {success:false, error:'Could not resolve repository info from git remote (override via targetRepository in config).'} and tracker posts a comment containing the message (failSetup posts comment too). Note failSetup writes file too. Assert: result.success false, error contains 'Could not resolve', tracker.comments includes message.

B. **No PR found** (gh.findPRForTicket → null) → returns {success:false, error:'No PR found for ticket PROJ-123'}; file rework_setup_failed.md written containing the error; comment posted; error comment posted via reportActionError.

C. **PR details null** → error 'Could not get PR details for #7'.

D. **No branch name** (prDetails.head null) → error 'Could not determine branch name from PR #7'.

E. **Checkout throws** → error 'Failed to checkout branch'.

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

(2) Analyze every acceptance criterion; follow existing codebase patterns; read AGENTS.md if present; use project skills; never invent new patterns. (3) TDD (RED failing test first → GREEN minimal implementation → REFACTOR); tests go in the standard unit-test tree only (Flutter/Dart `test/`, Node `__tests__/`/`test/`, Python `tests/`), NEVER in `testing/` (owned by test-automation agents; if production changes break tests there, leave them and note the breakage in outputs/response.md). (4) Run git status, add .gitignore patterns for sensitive/untracked non-code files. (6) Write `outputs/response.md` as a concise PR description; post-processing handles branch/commit/PR.
